name: Tiger-class cruiser as converted to a helicopter cruiser (HMS Tiger 1972 / HMS Blake 1969)

published.source: en.wikipedia 'Tiger-class cruiser': 555.5 ft (169.3 m) oa, beam 64 ft (19.5 m), draught 23 ft (7.0 m)

references.name: [CB] HMS Blake (C99), starboard side, converted (photograph)
references.note: Starboard side from a little abaft the beam and above: stem px 1375, stern px 262 (1113 px for 169.3 m, 6.57 px/m on average, the stern nearer the camera). The stations in the model's header (and the landmarks below) are read off it with the foreshortening taken out along the hull, NOT to better than about 3 m. Shows, fore to aft: the Mk 26 twin 6 in on the forecastle, the 3 in Mk 6 twin on the bridge front, the bridge block, the lattice foremast with its pole, the two funnels, the mack with the Type 965 AKE-1 bedstead, the boats and davits, the hangar with its door aft, the flight deck over the quarterdeck.

references.name: [CT] HMS Tiger at Portsmouth Navy Day 1980 (photograph, from ahead)
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'HMS Tiger (1945) at Portsmouth Navy Day 1980.jpg', 1600 x 2206
references.note: From the port bow, close: the bridge block's window rows and its wide bridge wings, the lattice foremast with the Type 992Q, the lattice mast of the ship alongside is not Tiger's. For the reviewer.
